items.title: Stella Oliver Interview, 1959-04-22
items.q: Lee Collins and Dutre and Ori and the whole gang of mine have them sometimes.

ctx.x: That was the only way I know. I couldn't repay him in any other way. I had to be nice. And all I could do was just cook a big pot of beans and tell them all come over. And that's all they wanted. Beans and rice. And Lee Collins and Dutre and Ori and the whole gang of mine have them sometimes. And Joe liked company too. He liked company. He was very fond of company. And he liked for them to eat. But as I said, he wasn't a drinking man. He wasn't a drinking man at all. But he had, he had a hard time with it. He had…
Where did you live in Chicago? Do you remember which street it was about?

items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I went over there and so Miss Stella met right at the door with smiles

ctx.x: Yeah, and where was your job?

Yeah, they was working down there and there. Where was Joe playing then? Joe was playing in Lincoln Garden. Lincoln Garden. Louis was working at the Dreamland, and joined the band at the Dreamland. I mean Lil was working there together. So I come to Chicago and I joined Joe's band. Well Joe had George Fields and he had a big band. He had the kind of band that he had now. He had a corner player playing with a man by the name of Bob Schaffner. He went later to the plantation with Dave Payton. So with the band…
So I said, when did y'all go home?
